name: Learn clicker training
blurb: A marker signal that tells an animal precisely which instant earned the reward. It works on dogs, cats, horses, chickens and, notoriously, on humans.
gear: A clicker, or a consistent marker word
An animal willing to work for food
steps: Charge the clicker: click, then treat, thirty or forty times, until the sound alone makes the animal look for the reward.
Learn the timing — the click marks the exact moment of the behaviour, and the treat can follow a second or two later.
Learn to capture: click a behaviour the animal offers naturally, such as sitting or making eye contact.
Learn to shape: click successive approximations towards a behaviour that never happens on its own.
Add the cue only once the behaviour is happening reliably, never before.
Keep criteria clear and raise them one step at a time — the classic error is asking for too much too soon.
tips: A late click marks the wrong behaviour. Practise timing by clicking a bouncing ball at the top of its bounce.
One click, one treat, always. Clicking repeatedly destroys the signal.
proof: You shape a novel behaviour the animal has never offered before, using only the marker and rewards.
